newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures slash losses, end lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures slash losses, end lower.

text.p: Topsy-turvy trading left U.S. stock index futures sharply lower but well above day's lows.

The March Standard & Poor's (S&P) 500 futures slashed its biggest loss of more than 19 points in choppy afternoon turnover, supported by shortcovering and signs that fresh buyers may have taken advantage of the pullback, traders said.
They said pressure lifted after the close of U.S. Treasury bond futures pit trading, albeit at sharply lower levels. March T-bond futures settled down 1-23/32 at 110-28/32.
"People were buying, and the market rallied some four handles," said a weary floor broker in S&P 500 futures.
"I think there must have been new buyers (and) a little bit of bargain-hunting," he added. "In my own opinion, I don't think this stuff closed that bad, down 55 points in the Dow."
"Bonds closed way down but then people started to look to buy," another floor broker said of the action.
Some said stock index futures had been oversold on an intraday basis after the morning's steep, abrupt slide on hawkish testimony by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan.
Greenspan told the Senate Banking Committee that economic prospects are "quite favorable" but that he couldn't rule out pre-emptive tightening to head off inflation risks.
Greenspan also said the U.S. stock market's rise may be unsustainable and that caution was warranted.
The remarks quickly slammed U.S. Treasury bond futures to about a 1-24/32 loss, while March S&P 500s immediately slumped their 15-point initial down limit.
Selling abated during late morning and early afternoon trade but revived again toward the close of T-bond futures.
S&P 500 futures followed suit and briefly built on their already hefty losses before the final bout of buying.
March S&P 500s respected the bottom of a key support zone spanning about 798 to 795, the first floor broker said.
Depending on how T-bond futures and overseas stock markets act overnight and the response to January's U.S. durable goods figures Thursday, stocks could recoup some losses, he said.
"You may see a little bit of a rebound," he added.
Durable goods orders are expected to rise 1.5 percent and gain 2.2 percent without defense orders.

Jay Hohmann, head stock index futures trader at Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette, said Greenspan's remarks provided a convenient excuse to retrace part of the strong recent gains in the cash S&P 500 index, and he said more downside was likely soon based on technicals.
Hohmann looked for the cash S&P 500s index to find first support in the 790 to upper-780s area, an old breakout point.
"So I think we have a level here...that still needs to be tested," he added.

March S&P 500s settled down 10.40 points at 803.75, Value Lines lost 5.50 points at 714.00, Nikkei fell 335.0 points to 18,835.0, Midcap fell 3.00 to 265.35, NYSE Composite dropped 5.20 to 421.35, Russell fell 3.50 to 364.00, and Nasdaq 100 lost 4.00 to 880.50.
